classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the repeated expression x²−2x as one quantity, factor the resulting quadratic, then translate both branches back into monic quadratics and retain all four roots. The preceding question cues treating an expression as a quadratic variable.

answer.short:
$x=-2,-1,3,4$.

Treat the equation as a quadratic in $x^2-2x$, then solve the two resulting equations.
answer.worked:
Let $u=x^2-2x$.

$$\begin{align*}u^2-11u+24&=0\\(u-3)(u-8)&=0\\u&=3\text{ or }u=8\end{align*}$$

For $u=3$:

$$\begin{align*}x^2-2x&=3\\x^2-2x-3&=0\\(x-3)(x+1)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }x=-1\end{align*}$$

For $u=8$:

$$\begin{align*}x^2-2x&=8\\x^2-2x-8&=0\\(x-4)(x+2)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }x=-2\end{align*}$$

The solutions are $x=-2,-1,3,4$.
